project_overview.purpose: Cloud-hosted retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system that answers customer and internal support questions by retrieving relevant passages from support docs, product docs, and release notes, then generating grounded answers with citations
project_overview.target_users: External customers using self-serve support chat, internal support agents using an assisted-answer sidebar, and product/docs teams who own the underlying content
project_overview.deployment_environment: Cloud, multi-tenant SaaS deployment on AWS, single region (us-east-1) for MVP with multi-region as a post-launch consideration

core_features: Document Ingestion Service (Python): pulls source docs from pdf, document, Confluence, Zendesk help center, and a Git-based docs repo; normalizes to Markdown/plaintext, chunks, and tags with source metadata (product area, doc type, last-updated date); flags low-quality parses at ingestion time using chunk-length outlier detection and non-text-content ratio (tables/images stripped to near-empty text), routing flagged docs to a review queue instead of silently indexing them
Embedding Service (Python): generates vector embeddings for each chunk using a hosted embedding model API; re-embeds on content change, not on a fixed schedule
Vector Store (managed, e.g. Pinecone/pgvector-on-RDS): stores chunk embeddings + metadata; supports metadata-filtered similarity search (e.g. restrict to a given product area)

Retrieval Service (Python): given a user query, retrieves top-k relevant chunks via vector similarity with metadata filters; supports hybrid search (vector + keyword) to catch exact-match queries (error codes, API names); computes a confidence score from top-k similarity scores and gates generation on a minimum threshold

Generation Service (Python, hosted LLM API): constructs a grounded prompt from retrieved chunks + query, generates an answer with inline citations back to source docs; skipped in favor of escalation when Retrieval Service confidence is below threshold

Escalation Handler (Node.js): triggered when retrieval confidence is low or generation is skipped; for customer chat, hands off to a Zendesk support ticket pre-filled with the query and top retrieved (but low-confidence) chunks; for the agent sidebar, surfaces raw retrieved snippets without a synthesized answer, leaving the agent to work from source material directly
Feedback Service (Node.js, PostgreSQL): captures thumbs up/down and free-text feedback per answer, linked to the query, retrieved chunks, and generated answer for later review

Evaluation Service (Python): runs against Feedback Service + retrieval logs on a scheduled batch job; surfaces chunks that are frequently retrieved but consistently thumbs-downed or never cited in a well-rated answer, flagging the source doc as a likely ingestion/chunking problem rather than a content problem; output feeds the Admin Console's stale/under-performing doc list
Support Chat Widget (React): customer-facing chat UI embedded in the help center
Agent Sidebar (React, internal): shows the same RAG answer plus retrieved source snippets to human support agents, who can edit/send or discard
Admin Console (React, internal): lets docs/product teams see which queries get the low-confidence or low-feedback answers, and which source docs are stale or under-retrieved
key_user_flows: Customer types a question in the support chat widget -> Retrieval Service fetches top-k chunks and scores confidence -> if above threshold, Generation Service produces a cited answer -> customer rates it thumbs up/down

Customer asks a question with no confident match in the corpus -> Retrieval Service confidence falls below threshold -> Escalation Handler creates a pre-filled Zendesk ticket and tells the customer a human will follow up, instead of generating an ungrounded answer

Support agent opens a ticket -> Agent Sidebar auto-generates a suggested answer with source snippets when confidence is high, or shows raw retrieved snippets only when confidence is low -> agent edits or sends as-is -> edit/send/discard is logged as implicit feedback

Docs team publishes an updated doc in Confluence -> Ingestion Service detects the change, parses and chunks it, flags the doc for manual review if the parse looks malformed -> chunk is re-embedded and updated into the Vector Store -> next query against that content reflects the update

Evaluation Service runs nightly -> cross-references Feedback Service ratings against which chunks were retrieved -> flags chunks/docs with a poor retrieval-to-positive-feedback ratio -> Admin Console surfaces these to the docs team, distinguishing 'likely bad chunking' (frequently retrieved, rarely helpful) from 'likely stale content' (rarely retrieved despite being about an actively-searched topic)
Product/docs team reviews Admin Console weekly -> identifies queries with consistently low feedback and ingestion-flagged docs -> flags the underlying doc for a content fix or re-ingestion
integration_points: Zendesk API (help center articles + ticket context)

non_functional_requirements.performance: Chat answer latency under 10 seconds end-to-end (retrieval + generation) at p95; ingestion/re-embedding of a single doc change under 5 minutes
non_functional_requirements.scalability: Must support burst traffic during product launches or incidents (~5x baseline query volume) without manual scaling intervention; corpus expected to grow from ~5k to ~50k chunks over first year
non_functional_requirements.availability: Target 99.5% uptime for the customer-facing chat path; internal agent sidebar and admin console can tolerate brief degradation
non_functional_requirements.security: No PCI/PHI data expected in support docs, but customer chat transcripts may contain account identifiers or PII incidentally typed by users; transcripts must be encrypted at rest and access-controlled; source docs may include pre-GA product info requiring tenant-level access scoping
non_functional_requirements.observability: Full trace per query: retrieved chunk IDs + scores, prompt sent to the LLM, generated answer, latency breakdown by stage (retrieval vs. generation); dashboards for answer feedback rate, retrieval hit rate, and stale-content flags

existing_systems: AWS (existing cloud provider for other internal services)
technical_constraints.budget_infra_limits: Hosted embedding + LLM API costs are the dominant recurring cost and must be tracked per-query; MVP budget assumes usage-based API pricing rather than self-hosted inference
technical_constraints.team_skillset: Small platform team (3 engineers) comfortable with Python and React; no prior production RAG experience, first system of this kind for the team

data_sources: User query + feedback logs (generated by the system itself)
data_architecture.storage_requirements: Managed vector store for chunk embeddings + metadata; PostgreSQL for query/feedback/audit logs; object storage (S3) for raw ingested source documents prior to chunking, to support re-chunking without re-fetching from source
data_architecture.data_flow: Source doc change (Confluence/Zendesk/Git/PDF/Word) -> Ingestion Service normalizes + chunks -> Embedding Service generates vectors -> Vector Store updates chunk + metadata -> user query -> Retrieval Service searches Vector Store -> Generation Service produces answer -> Feedback Service logs query/answer/feedback to PostgreSQL
data_architecture.retention_compliance: Chat transcripts retained 90 days by default, configurable per tenant; source doc embeddings retained until source doc is deleted or superseded; no formal compliance framework defined yet beyond standard SaaS data handling practices

open_questions: Should retrieval be scoped per-tenant (multi-tenant docs isolation) or shared across all tenants for MVP, given the initial customer base shares mostly the same product docs?
What confidence threshold triggers escalation, and how is it tuned?
Will it be a fixed similarity cutoff set by gut feel for MVP, or calibrated against a labeled set of known-answerable vs. known-unanswerable queries before launch?
Escalation handles the 'nothing relevant found' failure mode via the confidence gate, but not fabrication despite decent retrieval (the model citing a chunk that doesn't actually support its claim)
Should a post-hoc grounding check be needed for MVP, or deferred as a v2 concern once real fabrication-rate data exists?
Should the Agent Sidebar's edit/send/discard actions feed back into a fine-tuning or re-ranking loop, or remain purely observational for MVP?
How is staleness detected and surfaced? is a doc-changed webhook from Confluence/Zendesk sufficient, or does re-embedding need a periodic full-corpus reconciliation pass to catch missed events?
Evaluation Service's 'frequently retrieved but rarely helpful' signal needs a minimum sample size per chunk to be statistically meaningful?
What's the cold-start behavior for newly-ingested docs that haven't accumulated enough query volume to evaluate yet?
To improve the latency of the system, should we consider caching the top-k retrieved chunks of popular queries using sqlite or redis?
